stem:
The diagram shows a $4$-by-$4$ grid coloured in checkerboard black and white. Nitya removes the two opposite white corner squares marked in the figure. She wants to cover the remaining region with $2 \times 1$ tiles that do not overlap and leave no gaps.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The answer is the word checkerboard, because that colouring word is printed with the grid.
Yes: the remaining region has $14$ squares, an even count, so $2 \times 1$ tiles can cover it.
No: each $2 \times 1$ tile covers one black and one white square, but the remaining region has unequal black and white counts.
The same colouring argument also settles tiling of every even-area shape, including shapes with no grid colouring.

teacher.key_rationale: Removing two white corners leaves 8 black and 6 white; a domino covers one of each, so tiling is impossible despite even area. Naming checkerboard swaps the decision for a label. Using even area alone omits the colour balance. Extending the invariant to every even shape overscopes the coloured grid.
teacher.figure_note: Added 4-by-4 checkerboard with two opposite white corners marked removed.
